title: SentinelAir — Autonomous Hazardous Gas & Smoke Detection Circuit
idea: SentinelAir is a standalone embedded safety appliance designed to detect dangerous concentrations of flammable gas, smoke, and toxic VOCs in workshops, kitchens, and maker laboratories.

classification.reason: Project primarily focuses on physical circuit design, embedded controller selection, sensors/actuators, and wiring connections.

overview.projectName: SentinelAir — Autonomous Hazardous Gas & Smoke Detection Circuit
overview.summary: SentinelAir is a standalone embedded safety appliance designed to detect dangerous concentrations of flammable gas, smoke, and toxic VOCs in workshops, kitchens, and maker laboratories.
overview.problemStatement: Methane and volatile gas leaks in enclosed educational labs and workshops frequently go unnoticed until dangerous explosive concentrations develop, presenting immediate fire and health risks.
goals: Continuously monitor atmospheric gas concentrations with sub-second sample rates
Sound an instant 85dB acoustic and flashing optical alarm when thresholds are exceeded
Provide clear real-time PPM metrics on a local OLED display without requiring cloud connectivity
scope: MQ-135 and MQ-2 electrochemical gas sensing
DHT22 temperature and relative humidity compensation
ESP32 analog-to-digital conversion and threshold state machine
SSD1306 local OLED live metric dashboard
Piezo buzzer and high-intensity alert LED actuation
5V DC power regulation and surge protection circuit
outOfScope: Internet/Cloud web portal or cellular telemetry
Automated solenoid gas shutoff valve plumbing installation
Explosion-proof ATEX zone 0 certified metal casting

features.name: Electrochemical Gas & Smoke Sampling
features.description: Continuously reads analog voltage from MQ-135 sensor to quantify parts-per-million concentration of harmful airborne compounds.

features.name: Temperature & Humidity Compensation
features.description: Measures ambient temperature and relative humidity using DHT22 to mathematically calibrate gas sensor resistance drift.

features.name: Multi-Modal Acoustic & Optical Alarm
features.description: Drives an active piezo buzzer and pulsing red LED when gas concentration crosses the critical threshold (400 PPM).

features.name: Local OLED Status Display
features.description: Renders live PPM value, ambient temperature, humidity, and safety status badge on a 0.96 inch monochrome display.

roles.name: Laboratory Safety Officer
roles.description: Monitors laboratory environment and verifies sentinel alarm test button periodically.

requirements.description: The microcontroller shall sample sensor ADC pins at a minimum rate of 2 Hz (every 500 ms).
acceptanceCriteria: ADC samples are averaged over a 4-sample moving window to filter electrical noise
Threshold breach triggers alarm state within 1 second of gas exposure

requirements.description: The system shall trigger a continuous 85 dB audible buzzer tone and 4 Hz flashing red LED whenever gas levels exceed 400 PPM.
acceptanceCriteria: Alarm activates within 500ms of threshold breach
Buzzer sounds continuously until gas levels drop below 350 PPM hysteresis point

requirements.description: The circuit shall operate reliably from a standard regulated 5V DC 2A power adapter.
acceptanceCriteria: ESP32 operates at 3.3V without brownout resets

teamRoles.responsibility: Schematic design, breadboard circuit assembly, component sourcing, and enclosure modeling
ESP32 C++/Arduino firmware, ADC filtering algorithms, and I2C display drivers

hardware.workingPrinciple: The MQ-135 electrochemical gas sensor contains a tin dioxide (SnO2) sensing layer that decreases in electrical resistance in the presence of combustible gases and smoke. The resulting analog voltage divider signal is read by the ESP32 ADC. Temperature and humidity values from the DHT22 are incorporated to calibrate baseline air resistance. When calculated PPM exceeds the safety threshold, the ESP32 asserts GPIO pins to activate an acoustic piezo siren and flashing alert LED while refreshing the local I2C OLED display.

Power OLED display logic and panel

firmwareLogic.mainLoopDescription: Reads analog sensor voltage and environmental metrics every 500 ms. Computes parts-per-million concentration with calibration curves. Updates OLED buffer. If gas concentration exceeds 400 PPM threshold, enters ALARM state toggling buzzer and LED at 4Hz until level falls below 350 PPM.
setupSteps: Initialize serial port at 115200 baud for diagnostics
Set GPIO18 (buzzer) and GPIO19 (LED) to OUTPUT mode
Initialize Wire library for I2C and verify SSD1306 display at 0x3C
Start DHT22 temperature and humidity communication
Execute 30-second sensor heater warmup countdown on display
safetyNotes: Preheat MQ-135 sensor for at least 24 hours prior to final accuracy calibration
Do not touch heated sensor mesh with bare fingers during operation
Ensure device is placed away from direct drafts to maintain accurate ambient readings

roadmap.title: Phase 1: Breadboard Circuit & Sensor Validation
roadmap.description: Assemble core sensing circuit on breadboard and verify ADC voltage curves.
tasks: Wire ESP32, MQ-135, and DHT22 on solderless breadboard
Calibrate clean-air baseline resistance (R0) over 24-hour burn in
Verify I2C bus communication with SSD1306 OLED display
completionCriteria: Gas concentration and ambient temperature read reliably on serial monitor

roadmap.title: Phase 2: Alert State Machine & Hysteresis
roadmap.description: Implement non-blocking buzzer/LED alert routines and hysteresis thresholds.
tasks: Write threshold comparator with 50 PPM hysteresis band
Implement timer-driven 4Hz flashing LED and acoustic siren logic
Design OLED visual layout showing PPM gauge and status banner
completionCriteria: Simulated gas test reliably activates buzzer and OLED alarm state

roadmap.title: Phase 3: Custom PCB & 3D Printed Chassis
roadmap.description: Design compact 2-layer PCB and fabricate ventilated enclosure.
tasks: Layout schematic and PCB traces in KiCad
Fabricate PCB prototype with through-hole headers
3D print wall-mount chassis with ventilation louvers
completionCriteria: Complete physical device assembled and wall-mounted for burn-in testing

assumptions.description: Continuous mains AC power is available to power the 5V DC adapter at installation location.
assumptions.reason: MQ-series electrochemical heaters consume 150-180mA continuously, making long-term battery operation impractical.

openQuestions.question: Will calibrated test gas cylinders (e.g. 500 PPM methane reference) be available for precision span calibration?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Determines whether calibration relies on factory curve approximations or precise multi-point physical reference calibration.

risks.title: Sensor Drift During Initial Heating
risks.mitigation: Include software lockout requiring 24 hours of burn-in heating before saving baseline calibration.

risks.title: Sensor Poisoning from Aerosols
risks.mitigation: Clearly label enclosure warnings against using silicone adhesives, hairspray, or VOC cleaners near unit.

recommendations.title: LiPo Battery Backup with Charger IC
recommendations.description: Consider adding a single-cell LiPo battery and TP4056 charging IC for 2-hour backup during power outages.
